newsitem.title: UK: Majority of Scots want separate parliament - poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Scots want separate parliament - poll.

text.p: A clear majority of Scots favour a separate parliament with power to vary tax rates by up to three percent, according to an ICM survey published in the Scotsman newspaper on Wednesday.
ICM found 69 percent wanted a separate parliament for Scotland though support dropped to 59 percent on the question of tax-varying power.
Prime Minister John Major opposes any change in the 300-year-old constitutional link between Scotland and England but ICM found 38 percent of Conservative voters wanted a separate parliament.

The opposition Labour party promises a two-question referendum on the issue if it wins Britain's general election, which must be held no later than May. Seventy percent of those questioned by ICM said this referendum should also ask Scottish voters if they wanted independence.

An ICM survey of voting intentions published in the Scotsman on Tuesday showed the three Scottish members of Major's cabinet -- Defence minister Malcolm Rifkind, Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth and Trade minister Ian Lang -- could lose their seats at the election.

Labour would gain three to win 53 of the 72 Scottish seats in Parliament and Conservatives lose four of their 10. Nationalists would double their strength to six and Liberal Democrats would drop two to seven.
